    \newsavebox\pandoc@box
    \newcommand*\pandocbounded[1]{%
      \sbox\pandoc@box{#1}%
      % scaling factors for width and height
      \Gscale@div\@tempa\textheight{\dimexpr\ht\pandoc@box+\dp\pandoc@box\relax}%
      \Gscale@div\@tempb\linewidth{\wd\pandoc@box}%
      % select the smaller of both
      \ifdim\@tempb\p@<\@tempa\p@
        \let\@tempa\@tempb
      \fi
      % scaling accordingly (\@tempa < 1)
      \ifdim\@tempa\p@<\p@
        \scalebox{\@tempa}{\usebox\pandoc@box}%
      % scaling not needed, use as it is
      \else
        \usebox{\pandoc@box}%
      \fi
    }

    % For linebreaks inside Verbatim environment from package fancyvrb.
    \makeatletter
        \newbox\Wrappedcontinuationbox
        \newbox\Wrappedvisiblespacebox
        \newcommand*\Wrappedvisiblespace {\textcolor{red}{\textvisiblespace}}
        \newcommand*\Wrappedcontinuationsymbol {\textcolor{red}{\llap{\tiny$\m@th\hookrightarrow$}}}
        \newcommand*\Wrappedcontinuationindent {3ex }
        \newcommand*\Wrappedafterbreak {\kern\Wrappedcontinuationindent\copy\Wrappedcontinuationbox}
        % Take advantage of the already applied Pygments mark-up to insert
        % potential linebreaks for TeX processing.
        %        {, <, #, %, $, ' and ": go to next line.
        %        _, }, ^, &, >, - and ~: stay at end of broken line.
        % Use of \textquotesingle for straight quote.
        \newcommand*\Wrappedbreaksatspecials {%
            \def\PYGZus{\discretionary{\char`\_}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\_}}%
            \def\PYGZob{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\{}{\char`\{}}%
            \def\PYGZcb{\discretionary{\char`\}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\}}}%
            \def\PYGZca{\discretionary{\char`\^}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\^}}%
            \def\PYGZam{\discretionary{\char`\&}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\&}}%
            \def\PYGZlt{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\<}{\char`\<}}%
            \def\PYGZgt{\discretionary{\char`\>}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\>}}%
            \def\PYGZsh{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\#}{\char`\#}}%
            \def\PYGZpc{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\%}{\char`\%}}%
            \def\PYGZdl{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\$}{\char`\$}}%
            \def\PYGZhy{\discretionary{\char`\-}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\-}}%
            \def\PYGZsq{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\textquotesingle}{\textquotesingle}}%
            \def\PYGZdq{\discretionary{}{\Wrappedafterbreak\char`\"}{\char`\"}}%
            \def\PYGZti{\discretionary{\char`\~}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\char`\~}}%
        }
        % Some characters . , ; ? ! / are not pygmentized.
        % This macro makes them "active" and they will insert potential linebreaks
        \newcommand*\Wrappedbreaksatpunct {%
            \lccode`\~`\.\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\.}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\.}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\,\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\,}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\,}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\;\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\;}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\;}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\:\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\:}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\:}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\?\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\?}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\?}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\!\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\!}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\!}}}%
            \lccode`\~`\/\lowercase{\def~}{\discretionary{\hbox{\char`\/}}{\Wrappedafterbreak}{\hbox{\char`\/}}}%
            \catcode`\.\active
            \catcode`\,\active
            \catcode`\;\active
            \catcode`\:\active
            \catcode`\?\active
            \catcode`\!\active
            \catcode`\/\active
            \lccode`\~`\~
        }
    \makeatother

    \let\OriginalVerbatim=\Verbatim
    \makeatletter
    \renewcommand{\Verbatim}[1][1]{%
        %\parskip\z@skip
        \sbox\Wrappedcontinuationbox {\Wrappedcontinuationsymbol}%
        \sbox\Wrappedvisiblespacebox {\FV@SetupFont\Wrappedvisiblespace}%
        \def\FancyVerbFormatLine ##1{\hsize\linewidth
            \vtop{\raggedright\hyphenpenalty\z@\exhyphenpenalty\z@
                \doublehyphendemerits\z@\finalhyphendemerits\z@
                \strut ##1\strut}%
        }%
        % If the linebreak is at a space, the latter will be displayed as visible
        % space at end of first line, and a continuation symbol starts next line.
        % Stretch/shrink are however usually zero for typewriter font.
        \def\FV@Space {%
            \nobreak\hskip\z@ plus\fontdimen3\font minus\fontdimen4\font
            \discretionary{\copy\Wrappedvisiblespacebox}{\Wrappedafterbreak}
            {\kern\fontdimen2\font}%
        }%

        % Allow breaks at special characters using \PYG... macros.
        \Wrappedbreaksatspecials
        % Breaks at punctuation characters . , ; ? ! and / need catcode=\active
        \OriginalVerbatim[#1,codes*=\Wrappedbreaksatpunct]%
    }
    \makeatother

    \hypertarget{estandarizacion-de-la-base-de-datos}{%
\section{Estandarizacion de la base de
datos}\label{estandarizacion-de-la-base-de-datos}}

    En esta seccion se estandarizo la base de datos para que no haya alumnos
repetidos que inflen la calificacion promedio de un profesor, o de una
materia, etc. como los alumnos que revalidan materias y aparecen dos
veces en la base de datos. Por ejemplo, yo salgo 2 veces en Calculo, 2
veces en Calculo II, etc.

    Silhouette measures \textbf{cluster separation vs.~cohesion} on a
per-point basis and averages it.

\textbf{Glossary}

(d(x,y)): distance. (C(i)): cluster containing point (i). (a(i)): mean
distance from (i) to points in (C(i)) (intra-cluster). (b(i)): minimum,
over all other clusters \(C\neq C(i)\), of the mean distance from (i) to
(C) (nearest other cluster). (s(i)): silhouette of (i). \(\bar s\): mean
silhouette over all points.

\textbf{Definition}

For each point (i): \[
a(i)=\frac{1}{|C(i)|-1}\sum_{j\in C(i) j\neq i} d(i j) \qquad
b(i)=\min_{C\neq C(i)}\frac{1}{|C|}\sum_{j\in C} d(i j).
\] \[
\boxed{ s(i)=\frac{b(i)-a(i)}{\max{a(i) b(i)}}\in[-1,1],}
\] Aggregate with \(\bar s=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i s(i)\).

\textbf{Interpretation}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(s(i)\approx 1\): well inside its cluster far from others.
\item
  \(s(i)\approx 0\): on a boundary between clusters.
\item
  \(s(i)<0\): closer to another cluster than to its own → likely
  misassigned.
\item
  \(\bar s\) compares different (k): larger is better but it typically
  declines as (k) increases because clusters get tighter but also
  closer.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{For your plot}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Distance is the \textbf{KS effect size (D)}. Using
  \texttt{metric=\textquotesingle{}precomputed\textquotesingle{}} is
  valid.
\item
  The right panel says the cleanest global separation occurs at \(k=2\)
  \((\bar s\approx0.5)\).
\item
  For \(k\ge4\) the silhouettes flatten at \(\approx0.27!-!0.31\):
  clusters exist but are \textbf{overlapping}.
\item
  Combine with the elbow: choose the \textbf{smallest (k)} past the
  inertia knee that still keeps \(\bar s\) acceptable. Here that argues
  for \(k=2\) or \(k=3\) unless domain reasons require finer strata.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Practical checks}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Inspect the \textbf{distribution of (s(i))} by cluster. Low-median
  clusters are weak or too small.
\item
  Validate stability by bootstrapping prefer (k) with high median (s(i))
  and stable medoids.
\item
  If distances are non-metric or noisy also report \textbf{Wasserstein}
  or \textbf{energy distance} silhouettes for sensitivity.
\end{itemize}

\begin{quote}
``What is not measured is not managed.'' --- often attributed to
Drucker. \[
\boxed{\bar s(k)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i\frac{b(i)-a(i)}{\max{a(i) b(i)}},\ \text{pick }k\text{ maximizing }\bar s\text{ subject to an inertia knee}}
\]
\end{quote}

\hypertarget{imputaciuxf3n-de-faltantes-por-kde-truncado}{%
\subsubsection{Imputación de faltantes por KDE
truncado}\label{imputaciuxf3n-de-faltantes-por-kde-truncado}}

\textbf{Magnitud del faltante.} En la variable \textbf{CALIFICACION} se
observaron (3\{,\}217) valores faltantes sobre (26\{,\}140) registros
((12.30

\textbf{Mecanismo de ausencia.} Los faltantes no son aleatorios
(\textbf{MNAR}): corresponden a estudiantes con baja académica. Bajo
MNAR, el análisis por listas completas es sesgado; por ello imputamos
para mitigar sesgo de selección y conservar potencia.

\textbf{Soporte y criterio de truncación.} Restringimos el soporte a
\([\ell h]=[0,,7.5]\). Este rango coincide con la muestra operativa por
salón para estudiantes no aprobados y recoge heterogeneidad de
calificación por salón y periodo.

\textbf{Método de imputación.} Aplicamos \textbf{imputación única}
basada en un \textbf{KDE truncado} ajustado con los valores observados
(\mathcal O=\{x\_i:~x\_i\le 7.5,~x\_i~\text{no es NaN}\}). Para cada
faltante \(X_i\) se genera un pseudo-valor por ``jitter'' de la forma \[
X_i^{\text{imp}} \sim \left[\frac{1}{n_o}\sum_{j=1}^{n_o}\mathcal N(x_j h_S^2)\right]\ \Big|\ 0\le X_i^{\text{imp}}\le 7.5,
\] donde \(n_o=|\mathcal O|\) y \(h_S\) es el ancho de banda.

\textbf{Selección del ancho de banda.} Usamos la \textbf{regla de
Silverman} implementada así: \[
h_S = 0.9 s n_o^{-1/5} \qquad
s=\min\ (\hat\sigma,\ \frac{\mathrm{IQR}}{1.34}),
\] con tope inferior técnico \(h_S\ge 10^{-3}\). Aquí \(\hat\sigma\) es
la desviación estándar muestral y \(\mathrm{IQR}=P_{75}-P_{25}\) sobre
\(\mathcal O\). Cuando \(n_o<20\) se recurre a una \textbf{muestra
empírica con reemplazo} sobre \(\mathcal O\) y se recorta al rango
({[}0,7.5{]}). Si \(n_o=0\) se usa un valor constante de reserva
\(c=6.5\le 7.5\).

\textbf{Detalles de implementación.} Semilla reproducible
\texttt{seed=42} con generador \texttt{PCG64} muestreo por rechazo a
partir de índices aleatorios sobre \(\mathcal O\) y ruidos
\(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,h_S^2)\) los valores observados permanecen
\textbf{intocados} y solo se imputan las celdas originalmente NaN.

\textbf{Diagnóstico posterior recomendado.} i) Comparar observados vs
imputados en \textbf{media varianza y cuantiles}
\((P_{10},P_{50},P_{90})\). ii) Medir distancia KS o energy distance
entre ambas distribuciones. iii) Análisis de \textbf{sensibilidad}
variando la semilla y escalando \(h_S\) en \$\pm 10 iv) Si el objetivo
es inferencial, repetir con \textbf{imputación múltiple} \(m\ge 5\) y
combinar con \textbf{reglas de Rubin} para reflejar la incertidumbre por
imputación.

\textbf{Resumen operativo.} Faltantes \(=3{,}217/26{,}140\) (MNAR).
Imputación por KDE truncado en ({[}0,7.5{]}) con \textbf{Silverman}
\((h_S=0.9 s n_o^{-1/5})\); conmutación a muestreo empírico si
\(n_o<20\) y a constante (6.5) si \(n_o=0\); semilla 42; solo se
modifican NaNs; se recomienda validar con KS/distancias y, para
inferencia, usar imputación múltiple.

    We construct \textbf{pointwise bootstrap confidence intervals} for each
professor's KDE. Below is the complete method.

\hypertarget{glossary}{%
\subsubsection{0) Glossary}\label{glossary}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Sample \(x_{1:n}\): observed values of \texttt{IMPKDE} for one
  professor.
\item
  KDE \(\hat f_h(x)\): kernel density estimator with bandwidth (h).
\item
  Bandwidth (h): smoothing scale; we use Silverman's rule multiplied by
  your \texttt{bw\_adjust}.
\item
  Grid \({x_j}_{j=1}^m\): x-locations where we evaluate the KDE; we
  reuse seaborn's grid.
\item
  Bootstrap replicate: a KDE computed on a \textbf{resample with
  replacement} of size (n).
\item
  Pointwise CI at \(x_j\): interval covering \(\hat f(x_j)\) with
  nominal probability \(1-\alpha\).
\end{itemize}

\begin{quote}
``Resample your way to certainty, then admit the uncertainty.'' ---
anonymous
\end{quote}

\hypertarget{problem-and-notation}{%
\subsubsection{1) Problem and notation}\label{problem-and-notation}}

Given sample \(x_{1:n}\in[0,10]\), kernel
\(K(u)=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp(-u^2/2)\) (Gaussian), and bandwidth
\(h>0\), define \[
\hat f_h(x)=\frac{1}{n h}\sum_{i=1}^n K (\frac{x-x_i}{h}).
\] Goal: for each grid point \(x_j\) construct a \textbf{pointwise}
\$100(1-\alpha) \[
\bigl[L_\alpha(x_j) U_\alpha(x_j)\bigr]
\] that reflects sampling variability in \(\hat f_h(x_j)\).

\hypertarget{theoretical-frame-and-rival-models}{%
\subsubsection{2) Theoretical frame and rival
models}\label{theoretical-frame-and-rival-models}}

\textbf{Frame:} Nonparametric density estimation uncertainty via
\textbf{nonparametric bootstrap}.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Percentile bootstrap (used):} Empirical quantiles of bootstrap
  KDE values at each \(x_j\).
\item
  \textbf{Rivals:}
\end{itemize}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Normal approximation: \(\hat f_h(x_j)\pm z_{\alpha/2}\hat\sigma(x_j)\)
  using plug-in variance.
\item
  BCa bootstrap: bias-corrected and accelerated quantiles.
\item
  Simultaneous bands: e.g.~sup-norm bootstrap or Bonferroni across grid.
\end{enumerate}

Percentile bootstrap is simple and robust in finite samples normal needs
a reliable \(\hat\sigma\) and can misbehave near boundaries.

\hypertarget{mechanism-with-equations}{%
\subsubsection{3) Mechanism with
equations}\label{mechanism-with-equations}}

\textbf{Bandwidth.} Silverman with robustness to outliers: \[
h = 0.9\cdot \min\ (\hat\sigma \frac{\mathrm{IQR}}{1.34})  n^{-1/5} \text{bwadjust}.
\] \textbf{Bootstrap loop.} For \(b=1,\dots,B\):

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  Draw indices \(I_b=(i_1,\dots,i_n)\) iid from \({1,\dots,n}\).
\item
  Form resample \(x^{*(b)}={x_{i_k}}_{k=1}^n\).
\item
  Compute KDE on the \textbf{same} grid and bandwidth (h): \[
   \hat f_h^{*(b)}(x_j)=\frac{1}{n h}\sum_{k=1}^n K (\frac{x_j - x^{*(b)}_k}{h}) \quad j=1 \dots m.
  \] \textbf{Percentile CI at each grid point \(x_j\).} Let
  \({\hat f_h^{*(b)}(x_j)}*{b=1}^B\). Define empirical quantiles: \[
  L*\alpha(x_j)=Q_{\alpha/2}({\hat f_h^{*(b)}(x_j)}) \qquad
  U_\alpha(x_j)=Q_{1-\alpha/2}({\hat f_h^{*(b)}(x_j)}).
  \] \textbf{Split at threshold (t).} For visualization we:
\item
  Interpolate point estimate at (t): \$
  \hat f\_h(t)=\text{interp}(t;,x\_\{1:m\},\hat f\_h(x\_\{1:m\}))\$.
\item
  Interpolate bounds at (t): \(L_\alpha(t),U_\alpha(t)\) the same way.
\item
  Plot ({[}0 t{]}) segment with one palette and ({[}t,10{]}) with the
  other filling between \(L_\alpha\) and \(U_\alpha\).
\end{enumerate}

\hypertarget{cross-disciplinary-mapping}{%
\subsubsection{4) Cross-disciplinary
mapping}\label{cross-disciplinary-mapping}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Statistical computing:} Bootstrap resampling approximates the
  sampling distribution of a functional of the empirical measure.
\item
  \textbf{Numerical analysis:} We reuse a \textbf{fixed evaluation grid}
  to avoid interpolation bias in quantiles and ensure vectorized (O(mn))
  kernels.
\item
  \textbf{Signal processing:} KDE equals convolving the empirical
  distribution with a Gaussian kernel of width (h).
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{thesisantithesissynthesis}{%
\subsubsection{5)
Thesis--Antithesis--Synthesis}\label{thesisantithesissynthesis}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Thesis:} Percentile bootstrap provides distribution-free CIs
  that adapt to skewness in \(\hat f_h(x_j)\).
\item
  \textbf{Antithesis:} It is \textbf{pointwise} not simultaneous
  coverage deteriorates at boundaries and for small (n) (B) increases
  cost.
\item
  \textbf{Synthesis:} Use percentile bands for exploratory overlays if
  you need \textbf{global} error control or publication-grade inference
  switch to BCa or simultaneous sup-norm bands and add boundary
  correction on ({[}0,10{]}).
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{operational-steps-pseudocode}{%
\subsubsection{6) Operational steps /
pseudocode}\label{operational-steps-pseudocode}}

\begin{verbatim}
input: x (n) grid x_grid (m) alpha B bw_adjust
1. h = silverman(x) * bw_adjust
2. f_hat = kde$x_grid, x, h$
3. for b in 1..B:
 x_star = sample_with_replacement(x n)
 f_star[b, :] = kde$x_grid, x_star, h$
4. L = quantile$f_star, alpha/2, axis=0$
 U = quantile$f_star, 1-alpha/2, axis=0$
5. Plot fill_between$x_grid, L, U$ overlay f_hat
6. For split at threshold t:
 interpolate f_hat(t) L(t) U(t)
 draw [min t] with palette A, [t max] with palette B
output: pointwise $L, f_hat, U$
\end{verbatim}

\hypertarget{limits-uncertainty-testable-predictions}{%
\subsubsection{7) Limits uncertainty testable
predictions}\label{limits-uncertainty-testable-predictions}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage:} Nominal \(1-\alpha\) pointwise coverage. Not joint
  over all \(x_j\). Expect under-coverage near 0 and 10 due to boundary
  bias.
\item
  \textbf{Computation:} Cost (O(Bmn)). Reduce (B) thin the grid or
  pre-bin with FFT-based convolution if slow.
\item
  \textbf{Bandwidth sensitivity:} Bands shrink with larger (h) and widen
  with smaller (h). Prediction: doubling (h) reduces band width roughly
  by \(\approx \sqrt{2}\) in smooth regions.
\item
  \textbf{Diagnostics:} Repeat with \(B\in{200,500,1000}\) bands should
  stabilize. Compare percentile vs BCa BCa narrows where bias dominates.
\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{symbolic-recap}{%
\subsubsection{8) Symbolic recap}\label{symbolic-recap}}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  KDE: \[
   \hat f_h(x)=\frac{1}{nh}\sum_{i=1}^n \phi\ (\frac{x-x_i}{h}) \quad
   \phi(u)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-u^2/2}.
  \]
\item
  Percentile CI at (x): \[
   \boxed{ [ L_\alpha(x) U_\alpha(x)] =
   \Bigl[ Q_{\alpha/2}{\hat f_h^{*}(x)} Q_{1-\alpha/2}{\hat f_h^{*}(x)}\Bigr] }
  \] where \(\hat f_h^{*}(x)\) are bootstrap KDE values using the same
  (h) and grid.
\end{itemize}
